components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one primary action per view — the place energy concentrates.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-primary"><svg width="14" height="14" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M5 12h14"/><path d="m12 5 7 7-7 7"/></svg>Start session</button>
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; background: var(--color-accent, #0092ff); color: #fff; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; padding: 8px 16px; border: none; border-radius: 6px; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--color-accent-strong, #118cfd); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent-strong, #118cfd); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.6; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Recessed field: canvas background below the surrounding surface, subtle border, accent border on focus.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; background: var(--color-canvas, #0b0c0d); color: #fff; font-size: 16px; line-height: 24px; padding: 10px 12px; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.08); border-radius: 6px; outline: none; transition: border-color 150ms; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #9ba1a6; } .ds-input:focus { border-color: var(--color-accent, #0092ff); }

narrative.overview: Mesodapt is a quiet, dark instrument panel for the self-coached athlete. At rest, everything is measured and calm — near-black canvas, translucent surfaces, one type family, borders drawn in whisper-thin white alpha. The interface's job is to hold a lot of training intelligence without ever feeling loud, so the athlete can read their whole situation at a glance and act. The single blue accent is the one live signal on the board; its scarcity is what gives it authority. Energy is concentrated, not distributed: the visual world stays restrained precisely so the moments that matter — the next session, a plan proposal to accept, a completed set, a PR — land with force. Components lean tactile and energetic as their intended direction; the current build is more restrained (flat, hover-brighten only), so treat that energy as the direction to build toward from the flat baseline.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black canvas (#0b0c0d) with translucent white surfaces — depth by tone, never shadow.
A single blue accent (#0092ff), used scarcely and reserved for interactive/active state.
One type family (Geist); hierarchy from size and weight, no typeface switching.
Borders are white-alpha hairlines, never solid gray.
A separate data-viz zone palette (grey → blue → green → amber) reserved strictly for data.
Three-column app shell: workspace nav · contextual list · scrollable 756px content.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: The primary accent marks interactive or active state and nothing else. If two elements on a screen both wear accent, one is probably wrong.

rules.name: The No New Hex Rule
rules.body: Never introduce a raw color. If a design needs a shade the tokens don't have, add a semantic token (--color-<role>) first, then use it.

rules.name: The Data-Only Zone Rule
rules.body: The zone-* palette never touches chrome. If a green or amber appears on a button, border, or label, it's a bug — those hues mean data.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Every heading and body string is Geist. Hierarchy comes from size and weight — reaching for a second typeface is off-system.

rules.name: The One H1 Rule
rules.body: Exactly one page title per page, always via PageHeader, always with an uppercase eyebrow above it. The eyebrow is never bold and never accent-colored.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow for elevation anywhere in the dark UI. If something needs to feel raised, step it up the surface tone ladder (surface → surface-raised), don't shadow it.

rules.name: The Alpha-Border Rule
rules.body: Every border and divider is white with alpha (10% for border, 8% for border-subtle). Solid gray borders look muddy on the canvas — never use them.

rules.name: The Concentrated Glass Rule
rules.body: Planned material (not yet built): liquid glass is a signature material for the moments that matter, never a global skin. Apply it to elevated, decision-carrying surfaces — the accept-gate dialog, the Now/next-session card, a floating top nav — and never to data-dense regions where refraction hurts legibility and zone-* colors must read true. Scarcity is also a performance requirement.

dos: Do use tokens by role (text-fg-muted, bg-surface), never raw hex — add a semantic token before introducing any new color.
Do keep the accent scarce: reserve #0092ff for interactive/active state and the one primary action per view.
Do express elevation by stepping the surface tone (surface → surface-raised); keep everything flat otherwise.
Do draw all borders in white alpha (10% / 8%).
Do concentrate energy at decision moments — the next-session CTA, an accept-the-plan action, a logged PR.
Do use the zone-* palette for data marks only, -soft fills for large regions and full-strength for small marks.
Do render every page's H1 through PageHeader with an uppercase eyebrow above it.
donts: Don't add box-shadow for elevation — shadows read as smudges on the dark canvas.
Don't put a second accent on screen; if two elements both wear blue, one is wrong.
Don't let the zone-* green/amber/blue touch chrome (buttons, borders, labels) — those hues mean data.
Don't switch typefaces for hierarchy; Geist does everything, size and weight carry the levels.
Don't use solid gray borders, filled Lucide icons, mixed icon families, or emoji as icons.
Don't use fg-subtle (#9ba1a6) for critical information — it's for supporting labels only.
